title: The only lesson plan you need for your online drama classes
meta_description: Teaching drama online can be daunting, but not with our lesson plan and suggestions! We gathered a list of tested activities for a super smooth online drama lesson.

Zoom lesson plan for busy drama teachers
By admin
3 Sep 2020
2 Comments
September brings us all back to school, and even though the COVID-19 situation is slowly easing (at least in Hong Kong) we are certain that we won’t have any face-to-face classes for another two weeks at least.
Things are tough for every teacher and educator out there, particularly for drama instructors and coaches who must give drama lessons on Zoom, and therefore have creative solutions under their belt at all times.
If you, like many, are struggling for drama ideas for your online drama workshop, look no further: these ideas have been tested and tried out on Hong Kong students, and we think you should try them out on your next class too!
Online drama teaching ain’t easy, but you’ll be fine with our lesson plan!
Start with 10-15 minutes of warm-up activities. It puts everyone in focus and in the right mood.
For younger students (primary school or earlier):
Choose a happy, cheerful song. Ask your students to stand up and remain visible in front of the camera. They can move around, but they need to make sure they stay in front of the camera.
When the music stops, ask them to strike a different pose every time there is a moment of silence.
Songs recommended: Happy or Uptown Funk
Ask your students to walk around the room and give them different scenarios:
Walking straight, normally
Walking very fast
Walking super slow
Walking backwards
Walking on thin slippery ice
Walking on soft marshmallows
Walking on hot sand
Walking on quicksand
Walking on a rope bridge
It’s important for them to remain visible, so make sure they don’t disappear from your sight.
Explore the five senses through different actions. Guide your students through different situations:
Touching:
A hot stove
Icicles
Sharp glass
Velvet
An emery board
Tasting:
Sour lemon
Favourite candy
Spinach
Cough syrup
Super-salty soup
Hearing:
A gentle wind
A jackhammer
A loud crash
Classical music
Nails on a chalkboard
Seeing:
A car coming from far away and towards you
A giant
A big spider
A kitten/puppy
Zombies
Smell:
Biscuits
Perfume
Rotten fish
Onions
Bleach
Put your students in pairs. Decide who is the leader first, and the follower.
Together they have to mirror each other. Encourage them to make some vocal sounds too, so that the Zoom camera can follow them better. Or, if you prefer, you can put students, two by two, in breakout rooms. After a minute or two, let them swap roles.
Who’s in for a smooth online students’ activity?
Once your students are warmed up enough, you can start with the core activity of the day: monologues through storytelling.
Ask them to come up with a story, a real one. It can be something that happened to them or to someone they know.
If they go blank and can’t think of anything, you can help them select a theme:
Best holiday ever
Best birthday ever
The most embarrassing moment
Death of a pet
The moment I felt so proud
A big fight
Once your students have chosen their story to tell, select two of them. Student A will tell their story first, and student B will listen. Once A finishes, B must choose one of the characters in the story involved (very often there are at least 2-3 characters involved) and will have to retell the same story from that character’s point of view. Student B should not change the story and can ask questions if things are not clear.
Once they finish, student B can tell their own story (the one they previously selected) to a new student. Repeat as above.
Tell your students they just created monologues. This exercise will blow their mind.
Drama teachers: don’t let the situation stop your creativity!
Please let us know if your try any of these activities, and how they work out for your classroom and students. We’d love to hear your feedback!
